sentences.text: Brief facts of the case are that on 17.03.2020 Prabhakar Singh was traveling from Gautam Nagar to Badarpur on motorcycle.

When he reached the red light at Ali Road before Badarpur Flyover, a vehicle (Taxi) no. DL-1ZC-1603 (hereinafter referred to the offending vehicle) came at a very high speed, driven in a rash and negligent manner and hit the victim.
Due to this victim fell and sustained injuries.
He was removed to AIIMS Trauma Center.
3. An FIR no.88/2020, dated 18.03.2020 was registered u/s 279/337 IPC at PS Badarpur, District South-East.
Police investigated the matter and filed a chargesheet u/s 279/338 of IPC before concerned criminal court while DAR was filed before this Tribunal.
4. As per record, the offending vehicle was driven by MACT no.863/2024 Prabhakar Singh vs. Anil Kwatra & ors.

6. Written statement /reply was filed by respondent no.3 refuting its liability to compensate the petitioners pleading that respondent no.2 was in breach of the terms of the insurance policy in as much as respondent no.1 was not holding a valid driving licence on the date of accident.
7. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed on 05.11.2024.

sentences.text: Petitioner has claimed to be working as a sales executive at Rahul Medicos and earning approximate Rs.25,000/- per month.
Petitioner has filed his Identity card as Ex.PW1/4, however has not placed on record any proof of his employment or salary nor any proof of educational qualification has been filed.
The employer has also not been examined.
In absence of any proof of employment, income of the petitioner has to be assessed as minimum wages of unskilled labour.
The minimum wages that prevailed in the state of Delhi (address reflected as Delhi as per Aadhar card) on the date of accident were Rs.14,806/- per month.

As per discharge summary prepared at JPN Apex Trauma Center (AIIMS) and the medical record,
petitioner suffered grievous injury i.e. fracture in right upper arm bone (humerus) with I/C Extension.
Medical record reveals his period of hospitalization (from 18.03.2020 to 22.03.2020) as five days.
Though, no proof of loss of income on account of 5 days hospitalization has been filed.

Considering the nature of injury, period of hospitalization and the fact that petitioner also underwent surgery for rod implantation, it is assumed that the petitioner may have been incapacitated from working for at least 6 months.
Hence, the loss of income would have been for two months i.e. Rs.14,806X6=Rs.88,836/-.
